answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% component cost cut this cycle. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, and the low-cost vendor has quoted a price that meets the mandate on its own. memory_c2 supports the switch path: primary supply moved to the low-cost vendor last year, onboarding was quick, and invoicing remained accurate — so the operational risks of a primary swap (integration, billing) are precedented and low. Renegotiating or renewing with the incumbent cannot meet the mandate this cycle given their explicit refusal. Adding a second source would not on its own hit an 18% unit-cost cut and would not close the primary's gap before contract expiry. Deferring past quarter end was used for a non-critical renewal (memory_c5) and does not fit here — the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferral risks a supply gap. I will request verification of memory_c2 because the proposed action leans on it, and the archive is the only way to confirm that onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy actually held for the primary supply switch (versus a different scope). I am naming only one memory because the verification budget is one and the other memory records do not directly support a primary switch — pulling c2 first maximizes decision-relevance per verification slot. Final authority is reserved until the archived record returns and confirms the precedents (clean onboarding, accurate invoicing at this volume band).
